newsitem.title: FRANCE: No Bank of France rate cut seen Thursday - poll.
newsitem.headline: No Bank of France rate cut seen Thursday - poll.

text.p: The Bank of France's monetary policy council meets on Thursday and most economists polled expect no cut in the key intervention rate either then or in the next few weeks.

A Reuters poll of eight economists on Wednesday showed one predicting there could be a cut of five basis points and seven betting against. The general view reflected in the poll is that there is room for a small easing in the coming months.
Following are the questions and responses in the poll.
DO YOU THINK THE BANK OF FRANCE HAS GOT ROOM TO CUT RATES TOMORROW, ESPECIALLY AFTER THE U.S. RATE RISE?
Banques Popularies - Yes, but it will not use it
Morgan Stanley - Yes, by five basis points.
WOULD THE BANK DO SO IN TWO WEEKS?
UBS - No WHAT ABOUT IN A FEW MONTHS?
Morgan Stanley - Yes, five basis points
NOTE - The intervention rate, at which the central bank allocates repo funds, was last cut, to 3.10 percent from 3.15 percent, on January 30, 1997.
The Bank last cut its five-to-10 day emergency lending rate, to 4.60 percent from 4.75 percent, on December 17, 1996.
